question_text: A local government official argues that the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) is not binding in the Philippines because it is not a treaty. Which of the following statements best corrects this misconception?

options.text: The UDHR is a binding treaty that the Philippines ratified in 1948.
The UDHR is part of customary international law and its principles are reflected in the Philippine Constitution and domestic laws.
The UDHR is enforceable only in countries that have signed the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.
The UDHR has no legal effect in the Philippines because it was not incorporated by a statute.
